issues: No integrity problem found. The diff changes only one line, DEPTH from 8 to 6. It does not touch the seed lines, the prepare.py import line, the data, the evaluation call or the summary printing.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. A shallower model runs more optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s, so a better val_bpb is plausible. The model dimension may be derived from DEPTH (as in nanochat-style scripts), in which case the width also shrinks. Either way this is a legitimate change.

I could not recompute z exactly. The candidate mean is 1.06545 (runs 1.0659 and 1.0650), so the gain is 0.02945 against the incumbent's 1.0949. For z = 4.395 the harness must have used a noise scale of about 0.0067. With only one incumbent run, that scale must come from a noise prior, not from the observed spread. The two candidate runs have a sample SD of only about 0.0006, so the gain is clearly larger than run-to-run noise either way.
Caveat: the incumbent has only one run (n=1), so its true mean is uncertain. Still, the 0.029 gap is large enough that accepting seems reasonable.
